name: Syringocystadenoma papilliferum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological diagnostic criteria for Syringocystadenoma papilliferum

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic papillary projections lined by two layers of epithelial cells with plasma cell-rich stromal infiltrate
Solitary or multiple verrucous or nodular lesions typically located on the scalp or face
Positive staining for cytokeratin markers consistent with adnexal differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with typical clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily histopathological; clinical features guide biopsy site selection.

laboratory: Histopathology showing papillary projections with dual-layered epithelium and plasma cell infiltrate
imaging: Dermatoscopic features: multiple papillary structures with vascular patterns
other: Association with nevus sebaceus in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Different histopathological features lacking plasma cell infiltrate

redFlags: Signs of malignant transformation (e.g., pain, fixation to underlying tissues)
references: Lever's Histopathology of the Skin, 11th Edition
Dermatology: 2-Volume Set, Bolognia et al., 4th Edition
